text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — control-plane/config-drift detected. Symptoms: console shows successful route updates but dataplane returning 502/timeout for paging routes to model-set 'gpt-slim-embed'. Affected tenants: acme-inc, edge-beta. Severity: P2. Bridge: <https://call.internal/bridge/213210|join>. Runbook: <https://internal/runbooks/controlplane-drift>.

maya: i’m on it, joining bridge. noted acme reported multiple 502 spikes starting ~06:08 UTC. tagging sam for dataplane logs.

sam: looking at dataplane logs now — i see a surge of 502s from the router at 06:07. initial grep: `502 backend_fetch_error` across hostnames paging-*. redacting tenant ids.

jordan: quick note — we just rolled out configflag 'kv-prefetch-v2' to control-plane at 06:00 for canary. could be related.

maya: good call. can someone dump control-plane config version vs dataplane config? i suspect propagation lag or a flag mismatch.

sam: grabbing comparison. short log snippet:
```
06:00:02 controlplane: release config v3.2.1 flags: [kv-prefetch-v2=enabled, batch-window=30ms]
06:05:58 dataplane-agent(host-a): applied config v3.2.0 flags: [kv-prefetch-v2=disabled, batch-window=30ms]
06:07:05 dataplane-router(host-a): ERROR backend_fetch_error route=paging model=gpt-slim-embed
```

maya: that shows it — control-plane thinks flag is on, dataplane still on previous version. hypothesis 1: rollout failed to propagate to host-a due to agent restart race. hypothesis 2: flag toggle requires a schema migration for KV cache that wasn't applied. hypothesis 3: routing fallback is misconfigured causing mismatched expectations.

alex: adding telemetry: console shows 99th pct latency jump from 120ms -> 1.2s for the paging route at 06:07. throughput unchanged. suggests behavioural/per-request failure not pure load.

maya: action items —
- sam: collect full agent logs for host-a, host-b, host-c for 05:50-06:15 (assigned)
- jordan: check control-plane rollout logs and which hosts acked v3.2.1 (assigned)
- alex: assess customer impact and open a customer incident note; contact acme support lead for ETA.
- maya: attempt controlled rollback of kv-prefetch-v2 rollout if we see replication failures.

sam: logs attached (s3): <https://logs.internal/213210/host-a.log.gz>. snip shows agent re-registration sequence at 06:05:47 and a transient 503 from KMS at 06:06:10.

jordan: control-plane audit shows 06:00 rollout started, 06:04 majority ack, but host-a showed NACK with 504 on config fetch at 06:05:58. cluster-proxy spiked there.

maya: that points to propagation gap. ok plan: 1) stop further rollouts, 2) roll back feature flag at control-plane, 3) if rollback isn't quick, temporarily route acme and edge-beta traffic to a compatible model variant or dedicated fleet.

sam: attempting API rollback now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags/kv-prefetch-v2/rollback -d '{"to_version":"v3.2.0"}'` -> started at 06:18. response: 202 accepted.

ops-bot: automation task created: rollback-job-213210-1, status: started.

alex: customer impact note drafted -> https://support.internal/acme/incidents/213210. acme reports 37 failed requests, some retries succeeded.

maya: monitoring: after rollback request at 06:18, dataplane host-a applied v3.2.0 at 06:21 and 502 rate dropped to baseline by 06:22.

sam: confirming: host-a logs: `06:21:12 dataplane-agent: applied config v3.2.0 (rollback)`, `06:22:01 router: 200 ok route=paging`.

jordan: leaving a short postmortem pointer: need to improve the control-plane -> agent handoff's retry/backoff and surface NACKs earlier to console.

maya: building in-thread timeline for RCA (will copy to docs):
- 05:59:50 UTC — control-plane orchestrated rollout v3.2.1 with kv-prefetch-v2 true
- 06:05:47 UTC — host-a agent re-registered (transient)
- 06:05:58 UTC — host-a failed config fetch (504 from cluster-proxy)
- 06:07:05 UTC — first 502s observed for paging routes, spikes to 4% error rate
- 06:12:00 UTC — on-call notified via pager (page 1)
- 06:18:00 UTC — rollback triggered from control-plane (maya/sam)
- 06:21:12 UTC — host-a applied rollback config v3.2.0
- 06:22:30 UTC — error rate returned to baseline, mitigation successful

maya: hypotheses to track in RCA: 
1) rollout propagation gap (primary) — root cause: cluster-proxy transient 504 caused agent to NACK
2) feature depended on an agent-side migration not present in v3.2.0 -> compatibility issue (secondary)
3) monitoring and alert thresholds too coarse for early detection (tertiary)

alex: customer impact summary for postmortem: acme-inc: 37 failed pagings, SLA degradation window ~ 14 minutes, no data exfiltration, functionality restored after rollback. we should offer a postmortem and credit per standard escalation.

maya: next action: sam + jordan to assemble logs and config diffs, deliver a short RCA draft in incidents/rca/213210 by EOD. alex to prepare customer-facing note and CS handoff. ops-bot please create RCA stub.

ops-bot: RCA issue created: INC-213210-RCA, link: <https://tracker.internal/INC-213210-RCA>. assignees: sam, jordan.

sam: grabbing logs bundle now and starting grep for any other hosts that NACKed. preliminary: host-b and host-c acked successfully. host-a is only affected node.

jordan: I'll add a post-deploy check to the rollout job to gate on agent ack ratio >= 95% before flipping feature.

maya: leaving oncall at 07:00 UTC. handing to sam for RCA followthrough and any followup mitigations. sam — you OK to take lead?

sam: taking lead. will post updates in INC-213210-RCA and ping when draft is ready.

maya: thanks team — nice coordinated mitigation. closing thread in incidents once RCA stub updated. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: note: incident closed (mitigated) at 06:22:30 UTC per monitoring.
